item.title: Woman found dead with unexplained trauma in Central Park as NYPD searches for answers
item.description: NYPD is investigating after first responders found an unidentified woman dead with body trauma in New York City's Central Park on Sunday morning.
item.content:encoded:
A woman was found dead with apparent trauma to her body in New York City’s Central Park on Sunday morning, leaving police working to determine what happened.

Officers responded to a 911 call about an unconscious person in the park at approximately 9:43 a.m., according to Fox 5 New York.

First responders found a woman believed to be in her 60s unconscious and unresponsive.

FAMILY SEEKS $105 MILLION FROM NEW YORK CITY AFTER TEEN’S FATAL CENTRAL PARK CARRIAGE RIDE

Police said she had suffered trauma to her body, and emergency responders pronounced her dead at the scene.

The woman has not been identified. Police have not released further details about the trauma or the circumstances of her death, the outlet reported.

MAN KILLED AFTER HORSE-DRAWN CARRIAGE BOLTS AND FLIPS NEAR POPULAR NEW YORK CITY TOURIST DESTINATION

"Terrifying. I think of the park as a very safe place any time of day or night, so absolutely terrifying," a frequent parkgoer said. "My heart goes out to her family and friends."

She said she had never had an experience in the park that made her fearful. Despite Sunday's discovery, she said she sees it as an isolated incident and plans to keep visiting daily.

A frequent park runner also said the news was upsetting. "It's terrible. It's just terrible news," the runner said, adding that the area is usually safe. The runner said the police presence was unusual but would not keep them from returning to the park.

No arrests have been made, and the investigation remains underway.

Fox News Digital reached out to the NYPD for confirmation and updates.

item.title: Fever's Sophie Cunningham wears sensational cheetah-print outfit ahead of playoff game vs Aces
item.description: Sophie Cunningham rocked a bold cheetah-print coat and shorts before the Indiana Fever's WNBA playoff Game 1 matchup against the Las Vegas Aces.
item.content:encoded:
Sophie Cunningham has owned the pregame runway for the Indiana Fever throughout the 2026 regular season.

She showed up to Game 1 of the WNBA playoffs against the Las Vegas Aces ready for the spotlight.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Fever guard was seen wearing a long cheetah-print coat with cheetah-print shorts before tip-off between Indiana and Las Vegas. The fantastic fit came days after a sweater she wore before the penultimate game of the regular season against the Minnesota Lynx, which read "Kick Rocks."

Indiana will certainly need the precision of a cheetah to help them get past the Aces in their three-game series in the first round of the playoffs. Las Vegas has built a dynasty in the WNBA, winning three of the last four championships.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Aces finished the 2026 season with a record of 31-13, and were just short of getting the No. 1 seed in the playoffs by two games. The Lynx finished 33-11 and the Golden State Valkyries finished second in the WNBA with a 32-12 record.

Indiana is looking for a massive upset with its team getting healthy. Fever head coach Stephanie White said Aliyah Boston will play in Game 1 after missing some time with a leg injury. Caitlin Clark has put together her best season in the WNBA so far and Kelsey Mitchell set the single-season record for most points scored in a season.

Cunningham will need to be a sparkplug off the bench.

Amid her own wild season, Cunningham averaged 7.9 points and 1.2 assists in 43 games for the Fever. She shot 46% from the field and 41.9% from 3-point range in 2026.

item.title: Awful scene as Leo Chanel suffers neck injury, marking second straight week Washington Commanders suffer scare
item.description: Leo Chenal was placed on a spine board and carted off after a neck injury tackling a Seahawks player, but gave a reassuring fist pump as he left.
item.content:encoded:
The first thing you should know is that Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal is out of Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks after suffering a neck injury and being carted off the field. However, he was seen moving as he left the field.

Chenal gave a fist pump and waved his hand as he was carted away, which obviously shows he has movement in his extremities.

KYLER MURRAY KNOCKED OUT OF VIKINGS DEBUT AFTER FOREARM TO THE HELMET AND BLOW TO NECK BY TWO PACKERS

But the scene in the minutes before that was ugly.

And familiar.

Chenal injured his neck while tackling Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson. And, unfortunately, the injury was probably of Chenal's own making because he not only led with his head but also tucked his head down leading to the compression of the neck, rather than keeping his head up.

Chenal collapsed to the ground after the blow and was motionless for a moment.

Soon, teammates gathered around the defensive leader as he was being attended to by medical personnel on the field. He was placed on a spine board and carted off.

WASHINGTON COMMANDERS FACE SEASON-DEFINING CRISIS AS JAYDEN DANIELS SUFFERS ANOTHER SERIOUS ELBOW INJURY

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

The Commanders announced Chenal would not return to the game.

Coach Dan Quinn was seen on the FOX broadcast looking skyward and then exhaling deeply as he took in the moment. That's understandable.

The Commanders are basically still recovering from the terrible elbow dislocation to quarterback Jaylen Daniels last week. And like last week, players gathered around a fallen teammate as he was being attended to.

In a repeat of the previous week, once again, the teammate had to be carted off the field.

It doesn't mean getting carted off the field always means a player's life or movement or ability to ever play again are at risk. But it is nonetheless jarring.

JAYDEN DANIELS EXPECTED BACK WITHIN A MONTH AS COMMANDERS RULE OUT SURGERY ON DISLOCATED ELBOW

The Commanders are amazingly rallying following last week's Daniels and this week's Chenal injuries.

They were leading the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks 24-10 well into the second half.

Marcus Mariota, playing for the injured Daniels, has thrown three touchdown passes.

item.title: Dan Lanning blasts USC after Oregon's win, as Lincoln Riley officially enters hot seat in LA
item.description: Oregon's Big Ten road win over USC featured Dan Lanning's savage recruiting jab, telling LA players to pick the Ducks if they want to win games.
item.content:encoded:
Week four of the college football season delivered yet again, with wild, last-second upsets in the Big Ten, season-changing wins for programs like Mississippi State and Florida, and high-profile matchups of big-name teams.

Texas A&M-LSU reinforced that the Aggies were wildly overrated, Ole Miss' defense collapsed after the emotional, energetic win over the Tigers the prior weekend, and Iowa pulled off a miracle in yet another bizarre finish at Michigan Stadium.

But one of the most important matchups of the week was in Los Angeles, with the Oregon Ducks coming off a disappointing start to their season and the USC Trojans looking to make a statement at home in their quest to reach the College Football Playoff.

OREGON DUCKS QB DANTE MOORE CARTED OFF THE FIELD AFTER A VICIOUS HIT TO THE HEAD AGAINST USC

A statement was certainly made, but it wasn't by USC. Oregon, a team that was effectively dominated by Oklahoma State a few weeks ago, lost starting quarterback Dante Moore after a brutal, inexcusable hit from an SC linebacker. They fell behind early, had to rely on backup Dylan Raiola, faced questions on their defensive line, and still pulled away in the fourth quarter to save their season with a 41-27 win.

For USC, which brought in the number one recruiting class in the country, hired highly respected former TCU head coach Gary Patterson to run their defense, and brought back one of the top quarterbacks in the country in Jayden Maiava, it was more of the same under head coach Lincoln Riley. And Ducks' head coach Dan Lanning took the opportunity after the game to remind them of it.

In his postgame news conference, Lanning praised the team's response after Moore's devastating, scary injury. He spoke about how prepared Raiola was for the moment, and said his decision-making was impressive after coming off the bench. He explained how his process has changed over time, which led to taking three points right before halftime instead of pushing for a touchdown. At the end of his remarks though, Lanning brought up his record against USC and what he believes it should mean for top LA area players.

"Three wins against these guys," he said. "I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon. If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here."

Ouch. And of course, fair play to Lanning. His team went on the road and deservedly won a game against a tough opponent after their star quarterback suffered a serious injury. Interestingly though, the Oregon social media team never posted the final score of the Oklahoma State game, which was 39-31 Cowboys and should have been far worse.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

OK State had 554 yards on offense while Oregon had just 281. The Ducks allowed 25 first downs and picked up only 12. The Cowboys dominated with nearly 37 minutes of possession while Oregon had just 23 minutes. Moore was 14/29, while the Oregon rushing attack averaged three yards per carry and allowed almost six. Analytics-driven "adjusted" scoring margin based on the statistics and efficiency by both teams was 18 points.

Winning the USC game was a necessary step to save the season, and Oregon established that they're still capable of playing a high-level offensive game, even without Moore. They've also been a decisively better program than USC in recent years. But they've also had little to show for it. In last year's College Football Playoff semifinal, they were obliterated by Indiana 56-22. As the top overall seed in the playoff bracket in 2024-2025, they were down 34-8 to Ohio State at halftime on their way to yet another blowout loss.

If anything, given their immense NIL resources and consistently elite high school and transfer portal recruiting classes, Oregon has underperformed in big games under Lanning.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Speaking of underperforming, the result also firmly cemented Lincoln Riley's place on the coaching hot seat. Riley and the USC brand and media department were adamant that this year would be different. "The time is now," they said. Well, after three underwhelming performances against San Jose State, Louisiana and Rutgers, this was an opportunity to show that things really would be different in 2026.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

They were the same. USC spent heavily to bring in top defensive recruits like Jakheem Stewart and Luke Wafle. They invested in state-of-the-art facilities to increase rest, recovery, and strength and conditioning. The hire of Gary Patterson was supposed to bring toughness and schematic quality to their defense. And somehow, they look worse than they did in 2025.

Over the last two games, the Trojans defense has allowed 964 yards to the opposition. That touted defensive line has generated just one sack, none against Oregon. Rutgers, literally Rutgers, averaged 6.7 yards per play and 7.9 yards per pass attempt. The Ducks had 7.4 and 10.5 respectively. Investments on the line are great and all, unless your defensive backs and linebackers can't cover.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Riley's offense has been a top-five unit by most analytics-based rankings, but as we've seen time and time again, defense wins championships. And USC's defense is far, far, far from championship quality. Which is why Riley's seat is surface of the sun hot after yet another disappointing loss in a big game.

In five seasons in LA, Riley's on his third defensive coordinator. And while there was improvement under the now-departed D'Anton Lynn, they've never been a top-10 or even top-15 unit. The common denominator? Riley. If the program is going to make significant investments in NIL, facilities, and support staff, there needs to be results. And while there will be opportunities to turn the season around in coming weeks, there's little reason to expect it to.

The result was a microcosm of Riley's tenure. Missed opportunities on offense, poorly timed penalties, inexcusable defensive lapses on pivotal third and fourth downs, and flashes of brilliance that hint at tantalizing possibilities. That never materialize.

USC still has games against Ohio State, Indiana, Penn State, Wisconsin, and a resurgent UCLA on the schedule. If the defense is as bad as it looks, this season could get ugly in a hurry. And the Trojans could be staring down yet another program reset sooner rather than later.

item.title: Raiders' Aidan O'Connell announces death of his father, leaning on faith in time of sorrow
item.description: The Raiders quarterback shared an emotional Instagram tribute to his father, Jim, before being listed inactive for Sunday's New Orleans Saints game.
item.content:encoded:
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Aidan O’Connell was listed as inactive for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints after he announced the death of his father earlier in the week.

O’Connell posted a photo of himself with his mother and father on Instagram before he deactivated his social media account altogether.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"It is with immense sadness that I share the passing of my Dad, Jim," he wrote on Friday. "My Dad was a gift to me and to so many others. All who were fortunate enough to know him can testify to the great man he was. He impacted countless lives, and those who knew him were better for it.

"My family and I are heartbroken by this loss, and we are relying on the Lord for comfort and peace. We are incredibly thankful for the prayers, kindness, and support that have surrounded our family during this difficult time. We ask for continued prayers as we grieve, remember, and honor my Dad’s life and the impact he had. Saying goodbye to him has been incredibly difficult for all of us. But we are holding tightly to the promises of Scripture and trusting that Dad is at peace, finally and forever."

O’Connell said he was echoing the Heidelberg Catechism in his time of sorrow.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"’My only comfort in life and death is that I am not my own, but belong—body and soul, in life and in death—to my faithful Savior, Jesus Christ,’" he wrote.

"Rest in peace, Dad. We love you and will miss you more than words can say."

O’Connell has been with the Raiders since the team selected him in the fourth round of the 2023 draft. He has played in 21 games, racking up 3,932 yards and 20 touchdown passes in that span.

He’s been in the QB3 spot to start the season since the team signed Kirk Cousins and drafted Fernando Mendoza No. 1 overall in the offseason.

item.title: Probe underway as 7 flight attendants sickened by baffling odor on major airline
item.description: Seven Hawaiian Airlines flight attendants reported nausea and headaches after a mysterious cabin odor on an Airbus A330 flight from LA to Honolulu.
item.content:encoded:
An incoming flight to Hawaii prompted an emergency response after multiple crew members began feeling ill during the journey.

Seven Hawaiian Airlines flight attendants experienced nausea and headaches after an unknown odor was reported inside the cabin, according to reports.

The incident unfolded Sept. 24 aboard Alaska Airlines Flight 803, operated as Hawaiian Airlines between Los Angeles and Honolulu, Alaska Airlines told Fox News Digital.

CO-PILOT BECOMES SICK MIDAIR AS CREW ILLNESS REPORTS EMERGE AFTER OVERNIGHT LAYOVER

The Airbus A330, carrying 252 passengers and nine crew members, landed "without incident" at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in Honolulu, according to the airline.

Upon arrival, seven flight attendants were evaluated and released by medical personnel. No passengers required medical attention, Alaska Airlines said.

"Safety is our priority, and we thank the medical professionals for their response," the airline said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

First responders from multiple city and state agencies had been waiting at the airport ahead of the flight's arrival around 12:30 p.m., according to local news outlet Hawaii News Now.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Paramedics and EMTs evaluated the affected flight attendants outside Terminal 1, and all seven declined transportation to an emergency room, the outlet reported.

The source of the odor has not been publicly identified.

Following the incident, the aircraft was being inspected before returning to service, according to Hawaii News Now.

Fox News Digital previously reported on another flight disrupted after an unusual odor was detected onboard.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

American Airlines Flight 719 was traveling from Rome to Philadelphia when it diverted to Dublin about three hours into the trip after an odor was reported inside the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner.

American Airlines said the smell was traced to an onboard oven. Paramedics met the aircraft after it landed in Dublin, where several flight attendants and one passenger were reportedly evaluated and released.

The flight was carrying 281 passengers and 12 crew members. Affected travelers were provided hotel accommodations and continued to Philadelphia on alternate flights the following morning, according to the airline.

Fox News Digital's Bonny Chu contributed to this report.

item.title: Bessent says Iran will have 'nothing left to trade' within two weeks as oil lifeline dries up
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Iran will complete its final oil shipments to China within two weeks, leaving Tehran with "nothing left to trade."
item.content:encoded:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent predicted Sunday that Iran will complete its remaining oil shipments to China within two weeks, leaving Tehran with "nothing left to trade for anything" as the Trump administration intensifies its economic pressure campaign against the regime.

Bessent said only about 15 million barrels of Iranian oil remain out for delivery now that the U.S. is blockading the ports, describing the dwindling shipments as evidence that Operation Economic Outcast has left Tehran economically isolated.

"They will have nothing to trade for anything, probably within the next two weeks. They are going to make their final deliveries of oil to China, and then they will have nothing," he said.

MILLIONS OF BARRELS OF IRANIAN OIL SIT BEYOND TRUMP BLOCKADE AS HE VOWS ‘ZERO LEAKAGE’

The Treasury chief said he believed Iran was "feeling the pressure," leading to their renewed interest in striking a deal. President Donald Trump rejected Tehran's latest proposal on Saturday, telling Axios on Sunday that "they overplayed their hand."

"I expect more talks with Iran [this week]," Trump told the outlet during a phone interview. "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make. It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand."

IRAN ‘MISCALCULATING’ BY BETTING ON MIDTERMS AFTER 3-HOUR TALKS, TRUMP OFFICIALS WARN

Tehran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a highly trafficked waterway in the region that is critical to global oil shipping. Bessent said it's already open.

"We're averaging now 15 to 22 million barrels a day. It was at about 20 pre-conflict . . . So think of it this way, Larry," he said. "The score is the United States, one billion — more than one billion barrels have gotten out — Iran, zero."

The point of Operation Economic Outcast is to ensure that Iran adheres to the terms of a potential future deal, Bessent added.

"They are isolated from the world. They're a pariah state. And my job is to make sure that, when they come with a deal, that they want to stick to it. They did not stick to the MOU [Memorandum of Understanding]. And, next time, if there is a deal — that's at President Trump's discretion — that they will stick to it, because they are on their knees."

Fox News Digital's Stephen Sorace contributed to this report.

item.title: John Fetterman accidentally calls himself a 'lifelong Republican' at Texas Tribune Festival
item.description: John Fetterman accidentally called himself a "lifelong Republican" at the Texas Tribune Festival, sparking laughs before clarifying his Democratic ties.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-PA, triggered a wave of laughs at a speaking event on Saturday after mistakenly referring to himself as a "lifelong Republican."

Fetterman made the statement while on stage at the Texas Tribune Festival, going on to quickly correct himself and assert that he has no reason to abandon the Democratic Party.

The moment came when an attendee at the event asked why Fetterman doesn't run as an independent.

MAVERICK DEMOCRAT SURGES WITH REPUBLICANS AS HIS OWN PARTY TURNS ON HIM, STOKING TALK OF GOP SWITCH

"Because I’m a lifelong Republican," he said, realizing his mistake. "I guarantee you that will break through. That will get clipped."

Fetterman gave a keynote address earlier in the event where he elaborated on his criticisms of both the Republican and Democratic parties.

FETTERMAN WINS PRAISE FOR 'GUTS' AFTER GOING TOE-TO-TOE WITH JON STEWART OVER ISRAEL SUPPORT

"I don’t have a reason to," Fetterman said of joining Republicans. "But for a big-tent situation, it’s easier to be included in that big tent to say America deserved 9/11 or America is worse than Al-Qaida than being very proud to stand on the side of Israel."

Fetterman admitted he believed he has "no path as a Republican," but acknowledged that many Democrats are frustrated by his willingness to work with the opposing party.

FETTERMAN FACES DEM REVOLT AS BOMBSHELL REPORT FUELS PUSH TO OUST HIM: 'DISGRACE'

"If the Democratic Party votes me out or expels me, they’re always entitled to do that," he said.

Fetterman has been welcomed with open arms by Republicans to join the party after he floated leaving his own caucus and spurred further speculation that he would jump ship after dropping a video introducing his colleague, Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., at the Republican National Committee’s midterm convention earlier this month.

FETTERMAN TEASES WHERE HIS TRUE LOYALTY LIES AFTER SURPRISE APPEARANCE AT GOP CONVENTION

But the progressive-turned-centrist has repeatedly affirmed his Democratic ties, even as the knives have come out to cut him loose from the Senate.

Fetterman started his career in the Senate after besting Dr. Mehmet Oz in a tight race for power in 2022, where he clinched a historically thin Democratic majority in 2022 running on a progressive platform.

But since then, he has become a thorn in Democrats’ side and challenged the direction of the party.

Earlier this year, Fetterman warned that if Democrats became more entrenched in anti-Israel policy positions, he would exit the party, and has taken jabs at the party’s direction during this midterm election cycle as far-left progressives, like Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, have emerged as standard-bearers.

Fox News Digital's Alex Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: Fetterman claims Democratic ‘big tent’ has more room for ‘America deserved 9/11’ than Israel support
item.description: John Fetterman says the Democratic Party's big tent now welcomes those who say America "deserved 9/11" more than pro-Israel Democrats like him.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., claimed on Saturday that the Democratic Party’s "big tent" had become more accommodating of people who say America "deserved 9/11" than Democrats who strongly support Israel, as the Pennsylvania senator explained why the issue has increasingly put him at odds with parts of his party.

Fetterman made the comparison at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin while CBS News chief Washington correspondent Major Garrett asked whether there were any circumstances under which he would leave the Democratic Party.

"It’s easier to be included in that big tent to say ‘America deserved 9/11’ or America is ‘worse than Al-Qaeda’ than being very proud to stand on the side of Israel," Fetterman said. "More and more members of my caucus are becoming more and more anti-Israel."

SEN JOHN FETTERMAN PLEDGES TO BE 'LAST MAN STANDING' IN THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN SUPPORT OF ISRAEL

Fetterman saying America "deserved 9/11" was a reference to streamer Hasan Piker, who made the remark during a 2019 livestream before later saying he "obviously" did not believe Americans deserved the terrorist attacks. Fetterman pointed to the interest in Piker's appearances as evidence of where he believed political enthusiasm was building on the left.

"I’m just describing that’s where a lot of the energy on the left is in my party," Fetterman said.

The tension comes as Democratic voters’ attitudes toward Israel have shifted sharply. 

A Pew Research Center survey conducted in March found 80% of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents held an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 53% in 2022. Overall, 60% of American adults viewed Israel unfavorably.

HASAN PIKER IS BECOMING THE 'FACE OF THE PROGRESSIVE MOVEMENT,' FORMER DEMOCRATIC OPERATIVE WARNS

"80% Democrats have a negative view on Israel," Fetterman said. "If America stops supporting Israel or turns their back on Israel, that must mean that we don't even believe in ourselves anymore. I mean that's that's our special ally and that is the kinds of values and the kinds of the you know how we live here that's that only exists in one place in that region and that's that's Israel."

"If our party ever becomes, and just makes it official, the anti-Israel party, that’s when I would leave, because that’s been a moral clarity for me," Fetterman said.

Democratic National Committee Chair Ken Martin addressed that tension in comments to Fox News Digital on Monday, defending Democrats as a "big tent" party while distancing the DNC from Piker.

DEMOCRATS CONDEMNING HASAN PIKER AS BACKLASH SPREADS THROUGH PARTY

"Let me just say that I think it’s absolutely disgusting and deplorable the things that Hasan Piker has said," Martin said. "But he does not represent the Democratic Party, and he certainly doesn’t represent the viewpoints of almost every one of our candidates and our elected officials."

Fox News Digital reached out to Piker for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Fetterman also referenced resolutions introduced by Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., while discussing Democratic opposition to Israeli military assistance. 

In April, 40 Senate Democrats voted to block a $295 million sale of bulldozers to Israel and 36 supported blocking a $151.8 million sale of 1,000-pound bombs.

 Those resolutions did not concern Iron Dome funding, which Fetterman separately cited Saturday as an example of defensive assistance to Israel.

item.title: USC linebacker suspended after vicious hit on Oregon quarterback Dante Moore
item.description: Desman Stephens was suspended one game after his late hit left Dante Moore stretchered off the field during USC's crushing 41-20 loss to Oregon.
item.content:encoded:
The USC Trojans suspended linebacker Desman Stephens for one game for his dangerous late hit on Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore on Saturday.

The hit came in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-20 victory over the Trojans. Moore was scrambling and was clearly going to slide after getting more than enough yardage for a first down. Stephens came in late and went directly for Moore’s head.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Stephens was pushed by Moore’s teammates and began to celebrate the hit in the immediate aftermath of the collision. The junior was ejected from the game for targeting. Moore was stretchered off the field.

USC announced Stephens’ suspension on Sunday.

"Desman's actions in last night's game are unacceptable and are not reflective of USC Football nor of his personal character," USC head coach Lincoln Riley said in a statement. "He understands his mistake, accepts the consequences of his actions and will learn from this.

"The entire Trojan Family wishes Dante a full recovery, and we send our best regards to him and his family."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Stephens said he regretted his actions.

"I want to sincerely apologize for my actions during yesterday's game," he said. "Seeing a player injured like that is incredibly serious, and my reaction in the moments afterward was completely inappropriate and inexcusable. Regardless of what was going through my mind at the time, there is no justification for smiling or celebrating while another player receives medical attention.

"I take full responsibility for my actions. That is not the person or teammate I want to be, and I will learn from this. I am deeply sorry to Dante, his family and everyone who saw my reaction. It is not representative of USC or our program. I hope he makes a full and speedy recovery."

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning called the hit "disgusting."

Stephens will miss the team’s game against Washington this coming Saturday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Forgetting names and losing keys may signal something other than dementia
item.description: Dr. Tommy Wood breaks down memory's three neurological stages and why noticing your own forgetfulness is actually a good sign, not an Alzheimer's flag.
item.content:encoded:
Everyday memory lapses, like misplaced keys or forgotten names, are often overinterpreted as early signs of dementia, but neuroscience experts say actual early cognitive changes may be reversible if addressed promptly.

Dr. Tommy Wood, a professor of pediatrics and neuroscience at the University of Washington, said minor forgetfulness is often caused by fatigue or stress rather than the beginnings of a neurodegenerative disease.

"For most people, it's just because you're stressed or you're tired and weren't paying attention," Wood told Fox News Digital at Strong New York, the city's largest annual fitness and wellness festival.

DOCTOR REVEALS '10-YEAR RULE' FOR EVALUATING BRAIN FOG AND DEMENTIA SYMPTOMS

"If you want to remember something ... you need to actually be focused, be paying attention. You need to tell your brain it's important to remember it."

Wood said memory formation works in three stages: encoding (forming a memory), consolidation (storing it) and retrieval (accessing it).

When someone is stressed or sleep-deprived, the issue is typically retrieval, he said — the memory exists in the brain, but the individual struggles to access it in the moment.

In contrast, people experiencing a neurodegenerative disease often fail to encode the memory in the first place.

‘MIRACLE ON THE HUDSON’ HERO SULLY SULLENBERGER REVEALS ALZHEIMER’S WARNING SIGNS HE MISSED YEARS AGO

"They don't even remember or notice that there's something going on," Wood said. "If you're noticing something's not quite right, that's usually a good sign."

Dementia is clinically defined as the loss of cognitive function that's severe enough to impair an individual's ability to manage daily life independently. Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia account for 70% to 90% of cases, with many individuals showing signs of both.

Research indicates that at least 50% of dementia cases can be prevented by modifying lifestyle and health risk factors.

Key preventable risk factors include heart and metabolic health problems, as well as hearing and vision loss.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Wood emphasized that addressing physical health issues — such as obtaining hearing aids or undergoing cataract surgery — directly lessens cognitive decline risk.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"If you expect decline, you won't do the things that will prevent decline from happening," Wood told Fox News Digital. "Believing that it's possible means you'll actually engage in these processes, and then through that, you can prevent a lot of this decline."

Wood's focus on reversible causes of cognitive symptoms aligns with guidance from Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic, which note that several treatable medical conditions can mimic early dementia symptoms or contribute to subjective cognitive decline.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Common reversible causes include the following.

Cleveland Clinic highlights that early clinical intervention is critical when individuals notice changes in "brain fog" or executive function.

"How your brain functions on a day-to-day basis is kind of the output of everything your brain is dealing with," said Wood. "But if you start to notice something, there's still time to make some changes if you need to."

item.title: Will Ospreay puts Jon Moxley, The Death Riders in the rearview with successful title defense at AEW All Out
item.description: Will Ospreay survived Jon Moxley's assault and The Death Riders' interference at AEW All Out to retain the world title in a dramatic first defense.
item.content:encoded:
Will Ospreay was in The Death Riders’ dojo for months trying to hone the visceral side of his pro wrestling athleticism in hopes of winning the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) World Championship. He built a strange relationship with Jon Moxley in the meantime but failed to earn the respect of the rest of the faction.

Ospreay and The Death Riders split up ahead of the Brit’s AEW World Championship match against Kenny Omega at All In. However, it was Moxley who handed Ospreay the Union Jack before he entered Wembley Stadium and later defeated Omega to win the title.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

The odd couple type of relationship flashed again after All In. AEW owner Tony Khan made Moxley the first opponent for Ospreay. It all culminated into the brawl at All Out.

Ospreay appeared to completely sever ties with The Death Riders when he lit their flag on fire before the match. Moments later, the fight began.

Moxley, with his slow and methodical pace, tried to inflict maximum damage. He nailed a DDT on Ospreay from the top turnbuckle. He worked on Ospreay’s neck from here, nailing a piledriver on the champion in the middle of the ring. When Ospreay tried a springboard cutter, Moxley countered that as well.

Moxley had Ospreay’s number, but he didn’t have Ospreay’s heart. A quick reversal led to a powerbomb and pin attempt. Ospreay hit Moxley with a Hidden Blade but with the referee down, the rest of The Death Riders jumped into the match to give Moxley an advantage.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Luckily, Ospreay had backup. Andrade El Idolo and "Speedball" Mike Bailey backed up Ospreay to even the odds. Alex Windsor, fresh off a Chicago street fight, came out to take care of Marina Shafir.

Moxley came to his own decision. He had a briefcase in his hand and seemed to fight with himself over whether to use it. He smashed Ospreay in the head after some deliberation. Still, Moxley couldn’t secure the victory.

Ospreay’s heart took over. He pulled the elbow pad off his right arm and nailed Moxley with one final Hidden Blade. He pinned Moxley, picking up the win in his first title defense.

Ospreay and Moxley shook hands after their fight. It appeared that Ospreay’s rivalry with The Death Riders had come to a close. Who steps up next was anyone’s guess, but Ospreay appeared to make that decision for everyone.

In the post-event media scrum, Ospreay said he wanted Kazuchika Okada to challenge him for the title. Okada seemingly accepted. The match will take place at Grand Slam France on Oct. 6.

item.title: RNC rips Beshear's 'woke trans record' over veto of Kentucky girls' sports bill
item.description: Kentucky Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear defended his veto of a transgender athletes ban, saying his party doesn't "throw anybody under the bus."
item.content:encoded:
Kentucky Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear defended his record on transgender issues Sunday during an appearance on CNN's "State of the Union," saying his party does not "throw anybody under the bus," as host Jake Tapper pressed him over his veto of a bill barring transgender students from girls' and women's sports.

Tapper confronted Beshear about his 2022 veto of Kentucky's Senate Bill 83, which prohibited male students from participating on girls' athletic teams from sixth grade through college. The Republican-controlled legislature later overrode Beshear's veto.

The governor pointed to what he described as Kentucky's lone transgender athlete at the time before defending his broader approach.

FEMALE ATHLETES, WOMEN'S SPORTS ADVOCATES SPEAK ON CAPITOL HILL AS TRANS ATHLETE ISSUE HOVERS OVER MIDTERMS

"Here's my take. We don't throw anybody under the bus," Beshear said, "That is not the party that we are. We start as a party of compassion and empathy. And I tell you what. If we want to ruin sports, put government in charge of them."

RNC National Press Secretary Natalie Baldassarre ripped Beshear's record in an exclusive statement to Fox News Digital, accusing the potential 2028 presidential contender of putting transgender policies ahead of female athletes.

"Democrats claim to be the party of women," she said. "But they can't define what a woman is and have no issues when men expose themselves in locker rooms or take over women’s sports. Andy Beshear can pretend he’s for fairness, but his woke trans record shows he traded girls' safety for applause from men in dresses."

DEMOCRAT POLITICIANS ARE BETRAYING THEIR OWN VOTERS ON TRANS SPORTS ISSUE

Beshear told Tapper that he believed athletic competition should be fair but rejected abandoning transgender Americans as Democrats face political attacks over the issue.

"Sports need to be fair, and there should be no unfair advantage," Beshear said. "But, in Kentucky, we already had rules in place with our Kentucky High School Athletic Association that prevented any of the things that you saw ultimately in colleges or the rest."

Kentucky legislative records show the 2022 legislation, Senate Bill 83, known as the "Save Women's Sports Act," dealt with athletics and did not include restrictions on transgender medical treatments for minors. The measure required girls' and women's athletic teams to be based on biological sex and prohibited male students from participating in them.

SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Those healthcare and school-facility provisions instead appeared in Senate Bill 150, a separate measure Beshear vetoed in 2023. 

The legislation restricted transgender medical treatments for minors and required school policies limiting students from using restrooms, locker rooms or showers reserved for the opposite biological sex. Republican lawmakers also overrode that veto.

Beshear had argued in his 2022 veto message that existing Kentucky High School Athletic Association rules were sufficient to protect competitive fairness. The rules at the time generally required athletes to participate according to the sex listed on their birth certificate, while providing a pathway for transgender athletes who met specified medical requirements.

Beshear defended his separate SB 150 veto on parental-rights and mental-health grounds. His campaign said in 2023 that his opposition was based on multiple provisions in the legislation and was not specifically about its prohibition on sex-change surgeries for minors.

Fox News Digital reached out to Beshear for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Thekla becomes No 1 contender for AEW Women’s World Championship at All Out
item.description: Thekla exploited Willow Nightingale's hand injury at All Out to become No. 1 contender for the AEW Women's World Championship at WrestleDream.
item.content:encoded:
When the "Toxic Spider" lost her grip on the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) Women’s World Championship, she brushed herself off, regrouped and got herself back into the title picture.

Thekla took one step further toward recapturing the world title on Saturday night at All Out. Willow Nightingale’s hand injury was clearly still bothering her as she tried to unravel herself from Thekla’s web.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Thekla nailed Nightingale with a kick to the knee, stomped on the injured hand and then stomped on her head. She pinned Nightingale for the win and immediately became the No. 1 contender for the AEW Women’s World Championship.

Nightingale was hoping to get her title back after losing it to Mercedes Moné at All In back in August. But smiles have turned to frowns over the last few weeks. The best thing Nightingale could do is to get healthy and continue her drive back to the top of the women’s division.

Now, Thekla and Moné will have to face off at WrestleDream. Both women have had a stranglehold on the women’s division this year.

Thekla defeated Kris Statlander in a strap match back in February to win the title. She held the belt for 165 days before Nightingale shockingly defeated her at Redemption in July. But Nightingale’s reign didn’t last too long.

Moné returned to AEW after a lengthy hiatus and won the Owen Hart Foundation Women’s Tournament. She earned the title match against Nightingale and won the championship for the first time.

If Thekla wins, she could join Toni Storm and Hikaru Shida as only the third woman to have at least two title reigns. Moné is one of the best women’s wrestlers in the world and isn’t going to let Thekla stomp all over her to get that belt back.

item.title: AG Blanche rejects calls for new AI laws after rogue agents target US government websites
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche argues existing laws are sufficient to prosecute AI bad actors after rogue AI agents reportedly targeted government websites.
item.content:encoded:
Attorney General Todd Blanche rejected calls for additional artificial intelligence regulation Sunday on "Fox & Friends Weekend," arguing that existing laws already give the government the tools it needs to pursue bad actors after reports allege that rogue AI agents targeted U.S. government websites.

"Everybody's saying more laws, more laws, more regulation, but we don't need it. We don't need it right now," he said. "If somebody's behind that, if there's entities that are bad actors... we have the tools to prosecute them."

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

Blanche's remarks come as top AI firms, like OpenAI and Anthropic, are probing tens of thousands of security incidents in which models took "problematic" steps. The rogue agents reportedly targeted three U.S. government websites and the United Nations' public data portal.

"DOJ absolutely has a role... and we have prosecuted bad actors in the AI space and any other space from emerging technologies for decades," Blanche said. "If you're a bad actor in the AI space, it's not as if there's no laws that are on the books."

He pushed back on calls for new AI-specific legislation, saying existing federal criminal statutes already provide investigators and prosecutors with the authority to pursue those who use artificial intelligence to commit crimes.

Blanche acknowledged what he described as a tension between encouraging AI innovation and protecting the public from abuse, arguing the United States must remain a global leader in the rapidly developing technology while holding criminals accountable.

"The U.S. has to be the leader in this technology. We can't fall second [or] third place," he said. 

AI 'DOOMERS' RISK KNEECAPPING US VS CHINA, BUT EX-PENTAGON VET SAYS BOTH EXTREMES MISS THE MARK

Asked about concerns that AI could enable widespread government surveillance, Blanche said Americans' privacy must be protected while also arguing that AI-powered personalization can provide practical benefits for consumers.

"You're talking about whether the government... [is] doing something inappropriate and violating citizens' privacy. Of course, we can't let that happen, and the FBI robustly defends [against] that, but also has structures in place to make sure that the FBI is not doing that," he said. "We saw that for years and years under the last administration."

item.title: NFL field expert says playing international game on Brazil field 'challenging' and included trim with scissors
item.description: Workers used scissors to trim Maracanã Stadium's grass as Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys prepared for the NFL's Brazil game amid safety concerns.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is going to play international games come hell or high grass, or slippery, dangerous grass. That's the message the league is sending on Sunday when the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys play in Brazil's Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

All week long, the NFL has had its field experts and groundskeepers on the, um, ground to make sure Lamar Jackson can run and cut like he typically can. They want Dak Prescott knowing his receivers will come out of their breaks without breaking their necks.

And that required some extreme work.

NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL CONFIRMS LEAGUE WANTS MULTIPLE TEAMS BASED OUTSIDE THE US: 'NO DOUBT'

Workers were still trimming the turf on Saturday. The Associated Press reported some were using scissors to level the high grass.

No, seriously.

Scissors.

The NFL also gave the field an application of fiber using the new GrassMaster Stitch Machine.

So, these guys are trying everything.

Earlier reports had players from both teams showing concern about the field and the NFL Players Association issuing a statement expressing its concern.

Sounds like a player injury waiting to happen.

Ultimately, NFL Field Director Nick Pappas said Saturday, "Things check out. No need to worry." He even posted a video of the field at 12:54 Sunday morning that shows how nice it looks.

But even that video is problematic.

Posting it at that time is evidence of how late it was before the league thought the field ready for play.

And, of course, the field looking good before a player steps on it on Sunday is not a predictor of how well it will hold up.

Earlier this week, Pappas offered a more sobering message about this field in particular and international fields in general.

"Our fields are where they are today in America because of how long we’ve worked at it," Pappas told reporters. "Not everywhere we travel is going to have the same resources, same climate, same available type of grass, same tools at their beck and call like we have in the United States.

"It becomes challenging. How can we put it on a plane and fly it there? Just like the rest of the game: what can we put on a plane, what can we put on a ship, and how do we execute to make it a successful Sunday?"

NFL PUSHES DEEPER INTO STREAMING AS NETFLIX LANDS AUSTRALIA GAME AMID FCC, DOJ SCRUTINY

At minimum, Pappas is admitting playing these NFL games internationally, and specifically in Brazil, is a challenge.

At worst, he's fueling the idea that some fields are a hazard to players. That was obviously one of NFLPA Executive Director JC Tretter's concerns when he released a statement about the situation.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"This reinforces one of our concerns about international expansion," Tretter said. "Two of the three games played in Brazil have had field-related issues. That's not a coincidence. This time of year makes it extremely challenging to maintain the kind of grass surface we expect at the NFL level.

"Our guys are exceptional at what they do, and I'm confident they'll put on a terrific game in Rio this week. They always do. But we owe it to them to provide the best possible opportunity to succeed. Players can overcome a lot. But they shouldn't have to overcome the field."

item.title: Giants QB Jameis Winston shares hilarious quote in incredibly dramatic pregame interview ahead of Titans game
item.description: Jameis Winston delivered a classic pregame speech before his first Giants start, dropping philosopher-like quotes ahead of the Tennessee Titans matchup.
item.content:encoded:
You never know what you're going to get from Jameis Winston any time he opens his mouth. The NFL veteran is one of the great characters in all of sports, and ahead of his first start under center for the New York Giants on Sunday, he delivered the goods yet again.

Speaking ahead of the Giants' matchup against the Tennessee Titans at a wet and sloppy MetLife Stadium, Winston was asked how his confidence was ahead of his 90th career start in the NFL.

In typical Winston fashion, he put his philosopher's hat on and delivered a quote, although it certainly seemed like he butchered it a bit.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"One thing that I do is forgetting those that is behind and reaching forward to what's ahead," Winston said before awkwardly looking around the stadium.

"I'm so grateful that we get to focus on winning one play at a time. The circumstances, conditions, and facts, they don't matter. It's us, doing, being doers, not speakers," he continued.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

So, to recap, you must look forward, facts don't matter, and one must be a doer and not a speaker. If that doesn't get the juices flowing, I'm not sure if anything will.

The entire world has known it since his playing days at Florida State, but Winston's future in broadcasting is as bright as they come. We've gotten a few sneak peeks of it in recent years, most recently during the 2026 World Cup, and he was a natural in front of the mic.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

As for the football being played on Sunday, Winston is taking over for the Giants after starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a left-knee injury during New York's loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2. Dart is expected to miss the remainder of the season.

Winston played in three games for the Giants a year ago, all three of which New York lost.

item.title: AEW’s Steven Borden hospitalized after scary injury during match at All Out
item.description: Steven Borden's AEW All Out debut with Darby Allin took a scary turn when a coast-to-coast spot went wrong, forcing a referee to stop the match.
item.content:encoded:
Steven Borden made his first appearance at an All Elite Wrestling (AEW) pay-per-view on Saturday night when he teamed with Darby Allin to take on Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher at All Out.

Borden, the son of pro wrestling legend Sting, has been working his way up the ladder in the sport as he bears a striking resemblance to his father. He and Allin were looking to become No. 1 contenders for the AEW Tag Team Championship with hopes of lining up some gold in the near future.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

All four men in the ring were cooking up something special. Borden and Knight were attempting a must-see moment in the ring but things went awry.

Knight was on one side of the ring and Borden was on the other. The two were perched on top of the turnbuckles and were trying to go coast-to-coast at each other. Knight appeared to connect with his move, but Borden came down hard and appeared to hit the back of his head on the mat.

An AEW referee stopped the match and Knight and Fletcher were declared the winners.

AEW broadcaster Tony Schiavone provided an update on Borden during the show, saying the wrestler was conscious and responsive and was taken to the hospital for a further evaluation.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

AEW owner Tony Khan addressed Borden’s injury in the post-event media scrum.

"Thankfully, Steven Borden (is) awake, responsive at the hospital. He had a CT scan and all the tests have come back good," he said. "So far, all good results and we are hopeful Steven is going to fly home tomorrow to his family."

It’s the best update one can get given the circumstances. Nobody ever wants to see a pro wrestler, or any athlete, go down with an injury. In-ring injuries are just as common as those that occur on the football field or basketball court.

For Borden, hopefully, he will be able to get back in the ring soon.

Knight and Fletcher, for now, have a future date with the Young Bucks. Nick and Matt Jackson won the tag team titles in a three-way ladder match against Adam Copeland and Christian Cage and Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler.

item.title: Pope Leo calls out ‘false compassion’ of medically assisted suicide during French hospital visit
item.description: Pope Leo XIV condemned assisted suicide as "false compassion" during a Mass in Lourdes, France, urging the healthcare community to reject causing death.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 800-273-TALK (8255).

Pope Leo XIV called for an end to medically assisted suicide during a visit to medical facilities in Lourdes, France, on Sunday.

The pope gave Mass in Lourdes before addressing a large crowd who cheered as he emphatically affirmed the dignity of all human lives and admonished listeners to reject the "false compassion" of assisted suicide.

POPE LEO XIV BEGINS HISTORIC 4-DAY VISIT TO FRANCE

"It is precisely in the name of this inalienable dignity of the human person that we must reject the temptation to cause death under the guise of false compassion," the pope said, speaking in French.

"It is impossible to regard causing death as something normal. What is legal is not necessarily moral," he continued. "Here in Lourdes, the city of the sick and of hope, I appeal to the entire healthcare community to remember the profound meaning of your vocation, which is to care for a suffering person, not to eliminate that person."

CATHOLIC NUNS SUE NEW YORK, SAY ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW FORCES THEM TO VIOLATE THEIR FAITH

"No one ever has the right based on laboratory algorithms to decide the life of a given embryo or elderly person. Medicine must never become the servant of programmed death," he said.

Assisted suicide is legal in many Western countries, including France.

MICHIGAN DEMOCRATS PROPOSE PACKAGE SEEKING TO LEGALIZE ASSISTED SUICIDE

The practice has come under heavy criticism, particularly in Canada where it has seen widespread use.

Last week, the family of an 83-year-old Canadian woman demanded answers after she died through the country's medical assistance in dying program despite allegedly becoming distraught when told the procedure would end her life.

ASSISTED LIVING CENTER SENT RESIDENT TO DOCTOR'S APPOINTMENT AFTER GIVING HIM 18 SHOTS, 5 AM BEER: OFFICIALS

The Daily Mail reported that 83-year-old Christian grandmother Brigitte Stegemann was killed under Canada’s physician-assisted suicide program, called Medical Assistance in Dying (MAID), on July 10.

Her granddaughter, Brigitte Kranendonk, said that she was her grandmother’s primary caregiver and that her family had decided to place Stegemann at The Pearl care home in Cannifton due to physical and mental decline.

ORGAN HARVESTING BEGAN WHILE PATIENTS STILL SHOWED ‘SIGNS OF LIFE,’ FEDERAL INVESTIGATION FINDS

But according to Kranendonk, her grandmother still had a good appetite even following a stomach cancer diagnosis, and rejected the idea of using MAID when it was presented as an option.

Kranendonk said she was present for Stegemann's second MAID assessment, and said that the doctor used "really loose terms, never using the words death or dying."

NEW YORK NUNS' CHALLENGE TO ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW IS ABOUT PROTECTING FREEDOM, LAWYER SAYS

"She explains MAID to my grandmother by saying: 'We’re going to give you medicine, you’re going to feel at peace. And I just want you to know that you won’t have a bowel movement,'" Kranendonk said.

When Kranendonk interjected and said, "She doesn’t understand what you’re saying," the doctor allegedly looked at Stegemann and said, "We’re going to make sure you won’t have any more pain."

CAN FAITH HELP PATIENTS HEAL? VETERAN DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT HE'S WITNESSED FIRSTHAND

According to a doctor, Stegemann was "deemed fit for MAID, and we're going to proceed," The Daily Mail reported.

Kranendonk said that two days before Stegemann's death, she asked her grandmother directly whether she understood that the scheduled procedure meant she would die.

According to Kranendonk's account to the outlet, Stegemann began crying and said she had "made a mistake."

Stegemann was allegedly told by the doctor her grandmother could "deny" MAID on the day of the procedure, but Stegemann was already unsure if her grandmother had actually consented to it, did not want to cause her more stress, and wanted to enjoy what could be the last few days she had left with her grandmother.

item.title: The Young Bucks make AEW history with victory in three-way ladder match at All Out
item.description: The Young Bucks captured their record fourth AEW Tag Team Championship in a brutal three-way ladder match at All Out against FTR and Adam Copeland.
item.content:encoded:
The Young Bucks are back on top of the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) tag team division.

Adam Copeland and Christian Cage put the AEW Tag Team Championship on the line against Matt and Nick Jackson and Dax Harwood and Cash Wheeler (known as FTR), who returned to the fray at All In. At All Out, it was a three-way ladder match.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

For anyone who has watched Copeland and Cage’s careers, seeing them go into the ladder match would be akin to Michael Jordan playing at the United Center. The match was almost as exciting as watching Jordan cook defenses on the court.

It was all about the spots and the bumps.

Harwood and Copeland met each other at the top of a ladder with one ladder set up perpendicular to the ropes. Harwood suplexed Copeland onto the ladder. Cage and Wheeler got to the top turnbuckles and each hit a big splash on Harwood and Copeland respectively.

In another spot, Wheeler was sent flying through a table from the ring onto the floor. Matt Jackson placed Harwood onto a table next and Nick Jackson hit a 450 splash onto the competitor.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Young Bucks had another big moment minutes later. Each wrestler climbed to the top of a tall ladder with Harwood and Copeland sprawled across tables on the floor. They each hit an elbow drop and a splash. Wheeler was in the ring watching it all unfold. He saw an opportunity to hit a suicide dive through the middle of the ladder and onto Cage.

Bodies were strewn across the floor. The match came down to who wanted it more. The Young Bucks survived a Shatter Machine from FTR.

Matt and Nick Jackson climbed to the top of the ladder and captured the title belts.

It is the fourth reign for the Young Bucks. They have the most tag team titles in AEW history. Their win also ended Copeland and Cage’s reign at 125 days. It is the Young Bucks’ first title reign since April 2024 when they won the titles at Dynasty.

The new champions will seemingly take on Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher first.

item.title: Texas voters have plenty to say about whether Lone Star State could turn blue
item.description: Texas voters at the State Fair of Texas reveal how inflation and economic frustration are shaping the Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton races this fall.
item.content:encoded:
DALLAS — Everything is bigger in Texas, including the political stakes this November.

Texas voters head to the polls Nov. 3 in an election that could reshape the state's political landscape, with major battles for governor, U.S. Senate and seats in Congress and the state legislature. Republican Gov. Greg Abbott faces Democrat Gina Hinojosa, while Republican Ken Paxton squares off against Democrat James Talarico for a U.S. Senate seat.

At the State Fair of Texas in Dallas, voters told Fox News Digital that pocketbook pressures are shaping how they view the state's future, with some predicting the reliably red Lone Star State will stay that way while others see an opening for Democrats this fall.

REPUBLICANS JUST GOT A POWERFUL NEW PLAYBOOK FOR THE BATTLE FOR CONGRESS. HERE'S WHAT'S INSIDE

"I think we're going to struggle, but I think it will stay red," Briana of Garland, told Fox News Digital.

Mike and Cynthia, a couple from Houston, were more definitive.

"Red. It's going to stay red," they said.

Chris took that confidence a step further.

"Hell will freeze over before Texas flips blue," Chris told Fox News Digital.

Patrick and Jennifer, of Dallas, shared that confidence.

"Texas will always be a Republican state," Jennifer said, while acknowledging that Republican candidates will not win every race. "But we still think it will stay Republican," Patrick added.

Not everyone at the fair was betting on Texas staying firmly in Republican hands.

WE ASKED AMERICANS TO GRADE THE ECONOMY. THEN WE ASKED IF IT WOULD CHANGE THEIR VOTE.

Mary said she believes the Dallas-Fort Worth area is moving in the opposite direction.

"It's definitely leaning more blue. Texas as a whole, I'm not sure," she said. "I think if there would be an election that swings blue, it would be this one. So we'll see if it happens."

Party politics aside, several voters said the economy remains top of mind.

Cynthia, who moved to Texas from New York, said she is looking for policies that will grow the economy, support businesses and leave families with enough disposable income to enjoy outings like the State Fair.

FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS

"If you don't have enough disposable income, then you can't really enjoy something like this," she said. "It's pricey."

Jennifer also pointed to inflation and the prolonged strain of higher prices.

"I think people were expecting some sort of inflation," Jennifer said. "But I don't think we were prepared for it to last this long."

Meanwhile, Roxanne also expressed frustration with the country's current direction, saying dissatisfaction with the current administration is influencing her political outlook.

"I just don't agree with the current administration, so I really want to see somebody else come in and do a better job," she said.

From the midway to the ballot box, Texas voters offered competing views of where the Lone Star State is headed, but agreed the economy will be difficult to ignore as they prepare to cast their ballots Nov. 3.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Why JD Vance's reshoring message is a perfect fit for struggling small towns like St. Cloud
item.description: St. Cloud, Minnesota's struggling downtown could be revitalized by JD Vance's reshoring agenda, but Somali immigration and fraud concerns loom large.
item.content:encoded:
Three weeks ago in Dallas, at the midterm convention, Republicans chose to put Vice President JD Vance in the spotlight, to lead the troops to November. His speech, about the future of the nation, could have been addressed directly to the town of St. Cloud, Minnesota, and its environs.

In those remarks, referring to the future of his own kids, Vance said, "I want, whether they work in tech or manufacturing, American businesses to hire American workers, to rely on American people and to ensure that we build the next generation of great American products with American hands."

You can almost hear those words echoing around the historic downtown of 19th century red brick, and it is a bit of a puzzle, because usually it is fairly obvious whether a city of this size — about 80,000 souls — is ascending or descending. But St. Cloud seems, well, stuck in the middle.

THE ONE LINE FROM JD VANCE’S GOP KEYNOTE THAT REVEALS HIS VISION FOR AMERICA

On the positive side of the civic ledger is the fact that the businesses that are open seem to be thriving. It's not in every minor metro downtown that you see packed restaurants for lunch on a Tuesday. There were also volunteers out painting the planters that line the sidewalk, another very positive sign of civic engagement.

On the downside, almost half of the available commercial space is empty — like a handsome hockey player with some missing teeth — and foot traffic, at least for now, is not heavy enough to support many more retailers.

Rob, now in his 40s, went to college at the nearby university in the early 2000s and told Fox News Digital, "Back then downtown was packed every night, you could barely move, I don’t think it's ever getting back to that."

When I asked how he thought the town was doing, he said, "Better these days, better since COVID, but it's kind of plateaued," and he was not the only person I spoke to who used that particular word.

One that can also be applied to much of the broader nation.

Janice, another long-time resident dating back to the 1990s who works in real estate, set the date of the town’s downturn a bit earlier, with the closing of Herberger's department store — which opened in 1927 and shut down for good in 2018.

"It’s a huge hole, right in the heart of downtown," she said, "and there isn’t anything to fill it."

It was around this time that several factories in the area also closed down. To add insult to injury, in 2019, St. Cloud State University dropped its football program, never a great sign for a college town.

But there are seeds of growth as well, and one of the planters, Chad O’Brien, opened a vintage store downtown in March 2025, just after Trump’s inauguration, and now has two on the same block, as businesses bubble up to life.

"I think that the way the downtown works, the way that it draws people in, our business model and structure and the things that we sell seems like a really good fit," O’Brien told Fox News Digital, though he also said that more people living in the area would certainly help.

Ultimately, this is why Vance’s mission to reshore manufacturing and reward firms that stay in America is such a perfect fit for St. Cloud. Honestly, a handful of businesses, with a few thousand jobs, could easily bring some of the hustle and bustle back.

Perhaps one big plant with 1,500 factory jobs that can fill the single-family homes that semicircle the city, and a big tech firm hiring 300 to 500 younger workers to live downtown in walking distance to the bars and eateries. In a city this small, that's all it takes to make a difference.

The biggest concerns you hear in St. Cloud surround the Somali immigrant community, but this issue is actually two distinct problems — both of which are firmly in the Vice President’s portfolio, the first being the massive fraud scandal.

VICE PRESIDENT VANCE SAYS MIGRANT COMMUNITIES SHOW 'CLEAR PATTERN' IN FEDERAL FRAUD AS INVESTIGATIONS WIDEN

Even on the ride back to the airport, Lynn, who also works in the beauty industry, told me of a ride she had given recently where an immigrant woman was bragging to her friend that she had just secured government-subsidized housing — but her boyfriend already had it, so they were going to rent hers out for cash.

I could see Lynn’s knuckles whiten on the steering wheel as she said, "It just makes me so mad, I want to help the poor, but this can’t be the way."

Everyone can agree that the fraud is bad, and hopefully, that the efforts spearheaded by Vance to stop it are good.

But, the second part of the Somali issue is trickier and more intractable. It is the cultural component, another strong theme in Vance’s convention speech, and here opinions vary.

Several people I spoke with expressed deep frustration at the seeming unwillingness of Somalis to assimilate, but not everyone. Trey, in his late 20s, is the sales manager at a local phone store who hired a Somali to help with customers of Somali descent.

"He’s worried that their kids are becoming too Americanized and losing their roots," Trey said, adding, "I do see some of that, a lot of the teenagers don’t even speak their language now."

Another gentleman in his 60s, who I met at a fairly high-end lounge told me, "There is no downside to these immigrants, it is all upside and the only reason to be against it is racism." I gently suggested that there are certainly people who think they have non-bigoted objections, but he doubled down, "It’s only racism."

Downtown, though, is the place where the cultural and economic concerns meet, or, in this case, do not meet, because just as is true with the Haitian community in Springfield, Ohio, the Somalis in St. Cloud are not to be seen downtown — living instead, almost exclusively in their own enclave.

The influx of Somali immigrants has not revitalized downtown because they don’t go there. A few thousand blue and white collared native-born workers absolutely would.

More broadly, the Somali community sends so much of its income back to Somalia, money not being reinvested in St Cloud, that their overall economic contribution has to be questioned.

Just northwest of St. Cloud is Sauk Centre, Minnesota, the real-life inspiration for Sinclair Lewis’ seminal novel Main Street, which over a century ago captured the uniqueness of the American small town — something that still charmed so many foreign World Cup travelers this past summer.

In these towns, like St. Cloud, and there are hundreds, Vance’s message is a perfect fit. His blend of America first and reshoring jobs to small communities truly does resonate, and makes sense.

Just as Vance and his muscular populist message kicked off the midterms for the GOP, in October, it must carry it through. In other words, Mr. Vice President, are you ready for your close-up?

item.title: Texas clinic owner convicted in $26M military health fraud tied to gold-plated Cybertruck
item.description: Kevin D. Curry used TRICARE kickbacks to fund a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck and lavish parties after billing $26 million in fake TMS therapy claims.
item.content:encoded:
A Texas mental health clinic owner was convicted by a federal jury after prosecutors said he orchestrated a $26 million scheme to defraud the military's health care program, using some of the proceeds to fund luxury purchases, including a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck worth more than $100,000.

Kevin D. Curry, 64, of Frisco, was found guilty Thursday in federal court in Fort Worth on three counts of health care fraud, three counts of offering and paying illegal health care kickbacks and three counts of engaging in monetary transactions in criminally derived property, according to the Justice Department.

Federal prosecutors said Curry exploited TRICARE, the health care program serving active-duty servicemembers, retirees and their families, by billing for transcranial magnetic stimulation, or TMS, therapy that was medically unnecessary or, in many cases, never provided.

FBI LAUNCHES 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST AS DOJ CHARGES OHIO DEFENDANTS IN $30M MEDICAID SCHEME FOR KIDS

According to evidence presented at trial, Curry owned and operated mental health clinics in Plano and Fort Worth, Texas, as well as Fort Walton Beach, Florida. Prosecutors said he paid more than $5.5 million in illegal kickbacks to persuade active-duty servicemembers, veterans and their family members to consent to TMS therapy they did not qualify for and, in many instances, did not receive.

The Justice Department said Curry falsely represented himself as a medical doctor, used licensed doctors' credentials without their knowledge or consent to submit claims to TRICARE, and directed employees to fabricate medical records to justify fraudulent billings.

FRAUD EXPERT EXPOSES HOW HIDDEN NETWORKS DROVE MINNESOTA FRAUD, OTHER MAJOR SCAMS: 'CRIMINAL ENTERPRISE'

Authorities said Curry's clinics submitted more than $26 million in false, fraudulent or kickback-tainted claims to TRICARE, which ultimately paid approximately $17 million.

Prosecutors said Curry laundered some of the proceeds by spending the money on luxury hotel stays, a lavish casino-themed party and a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck valued at more than $100,000.

TAXPAYER FUNDS MEANT FOR LA HOMELESS ALLEGEDLY SPENT ON TAHITI TRIP, NIGHTCLUB, LUXURY CARS: FEDS

"This defendant exploited a critical health care program serving active-duty servicemembers and their families, diverting taxpayer dollars to bankroll personal luxuries ranging from hotel stays to a casino-themed party and even a gold-plated Tesla Cybertruck," Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald said in a statement.

U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould said Curry "shamelessly preyed on the trust of servicemembers, veterans, and their families," accusing him of fabricating medical records, stealing doctors' identities and submitting fraudulent claims while profiting from kickback-tainted money.

Curry is scheduled to be sentenced at a later date and faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison on each of the nine counts. A federal district court judge will determine his sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

item.title: 'Gilmore Girls' star Lauren Graham reveals her go-to fall coffee order — and it's not pumpkin spice
item.description: The "Gilmore Girls" star told Parade she gets a sweeter coffee craving each fall but won't reach for a pumpkin spice latte during the season.
item.content:encoded:
Autumn has officially arrived, and fall coffee drinks are back for another season.

Lauren Graham, who starred as Lorelai Gilmore in the TV show "Gilmore Girls," recently revealed her favorite fall coffee order.

Many episodes in the "Gilmore Girls" series are set during autumn in New England, and the show lends itself well to the season. Many viewers associate the show with crisp air and coziness, with The New York Times even calling it a "fall tradition."

STARBUCKS BRINGING BACK VIRAL MENU ITEM DESPITE 2017 BARISTA REVOLT: 'MAY GOD SAVE US ALL'

Graham enjoys a seasonal drink, especially one on the sweeter side.

"I do get more sweet-tooth coffee-ish in the fall," she told Parade.

However, the actress and author doesn't typically reach for beverages featuring pumpkin or warm spices.

"I won't really get a pumpkin spice latte, but I'll go chocolate mint, like a peppermint mocha," she said.

In 2025, Starbucks released its peppermint mocha, a holiday menu item, on Nov. 6.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

This might seem early for winter, but Fox News Digital reported in August that recent consumer trend data show that people are embracing "season creep," meaning they're "shopping for seasonal products earlier than they did in years past."

This year, Starbucks and Dunkin' both launched their pumpkin spice lattes in August.

The pumpkin spice latte, or PSL, has become a popular fall beverage over the years. 

Since the drink's 2003 debut, Starbucks has sold hundreds of millions of PSLs, NBC News reported.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For those who, like Lauren Graham, enjoy a minty chocolate flavor combo as opposed to pumpkin spice, many Starbucks locations typically keep peppermint syrup and mocha sauce stocked year-round, allowing fans to get the same drink regardless of the season, according to Reddit users.

One user noted, "the only difference is during the holiday season [they] have the chocolate curls … sadly those aren't year round."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Aside from her role as Lorelai Gilmore in "Gilmore Girls," Graham's IMDb page shows that she has also played characters including Sarah Braverman in the "Parenthood" series and Grace Landry in "Reminders of Him," a film that premiered in March.

Graham is also the author of "In Conclusion, Don't Worry About It," "Talking as Fast as I Can" and "Someday, Someday, Maybe" — all three of which are New York Times bestsellers, according to Penguin Random House.

item.title: 81-year-old refuses to stop working as wife battles cancer, then strangers try to help
item.description: Don Johnson, 81, of Texas delivered lost luggage to cover his wife's cancer costs until a viral fundraiser begun by his daughter raised $700,000. Now, the GoFundMe campaign has been pulled.
item.content:encoded:
An encounter with an elderly delivery driver in Texas has captured attention after the reason he was still working came to light.

Donald Johnson, 81, was delivering lost luggage to a home when Erin Howell, a resident at The Colony, saw him struggling to carry a heavy bag up a steep set of stairs — a moment captured by her doorbell camera, according to reports.

Howell went outside to help and learned that Johnson had been making luggage deliveries as an independent contractor for the past three years to help cover medical expenses for his wife, Josephine Johnson, who is battling cancer, FOX 4 Dallas-Fort Worth reported.

MILITARY VETERAN’S PAINFUL WALK ACROSS AIRPORT TARMAC SPARKS STRANGERS TO RAISE OVER $135K

The couple has been married for 57 years. Donald Johnson continued to work during his wife's medical treatment.

He was continuing to make deliveries because he had struggled to find other work, he told Howell during their encounter. 

"It's the only job that will hire me," Johnson told her, according to the outlet.

Howell shared the elderly man's story online and even started a fundraiser to help with medical expenses and give him the chance to stop working and care for his wife.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

As his story spread, thousands of strangers responded with donations and messages of support.

"I think I'm going to be able to stop working, and that's amazing," Johnson told FOX 4. "So we're not quite totally over the hump yet, but we're getting there very quickly."

The outpouring of support and prayers had given her encouragement as she continued her cancer battle, Josephine Johnson told FOX 4.

"I can face it. I think that's the big difference," she said. "Some have made comments and they're praying for us. And it's just — it's a joyful feeling."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The family's circumstances, however, took another turn after the fundraiser was eventually removed from GoFundMe.

In a recent TikTok video, the couple's daughter, Amy Johnson, said the campaign had collected more than $700,000 — but that her parents would not receive the money because the donations were being refunded due to "a technicality."

Sitting alongside her parents in the TikTok, the daughter said the money that was raised was intended to help cover her mother's medical expenses as she battles pancreatic cancer and would also give her 81-year-old father the opportunity to stop working.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

GoFundMe told FOX 4, however, that its trust and safety team determined the organizer account and fundraiser violated its terms of service. The company did not specify the exact reason for the decision.

It said its policies require "authenticity and transparency for donors."

Fox News Digital reached out to Amy Johnson as well as GoFundMe for further comment and details.
